questions.question: How does the proposed Galerkin-FFT algorithm impose macroscopic stress control without an outer correction loop?

options.A: Modify the projection operator's null-frequency component to the fourth-order identity, making the mean stress equal the target
options.B: Iteratively adjust the reference medium until the mean stress converges
options.C: Replace the conjugate-gradient solver with a direct finite-element solve
options.D: Prescribe a strain ramp and infer stress from a post-processing fit

questions.rationale: At zero frequency the modified operator retains the average tensor instead of annihilating it, enforcing the target stress.
questions.evidence_quote: defining its value as the fourth order identity tensor

questions.question: What changes at the null frequency for components under mixed loading?

options.A: Stress-controlled components use identity projection while strain-controlled components use zero projection
options.B: All components use identity, with strain values imposed by a penalty
options.C: All components use zero, and stresses are recovered from reaction forces
options.D: The operator is diagonalized using the material tangent

questions.rationale: The mixed-control projector assigns its zero-frequency blocks by the type of control specified per component.
questions.evidence_quote: if ξ = 0 for stress controled IJ terms

questions.question: Why does the stress-control Newton correction differ from the strain-control correction?

options.A: It includes a mean deformation-gradient correction as well as fluctuations
options.B: It is constrained to have zero mean while the stress-control mean is externally prescribed
options.C: It corrects stress directly and leaves deformation unchanged
options.D: It is computed without the material tangent

questions.rationale: Full F is unknown under stress control, so δF includes a mean contribution.
questions.evidence_quote: the correction for the deformation gradient field δF includes a mean value

questions.question: What computational advantage does the abstract claim relative to strain-controlled Galerkin FFT?

options.A: The method needs no additional iterations in either the linear solver or the Newton scheme
options.B: It eliminates the need for a Newton solver but doubles conjugate-gradient iterations
options.C: It requires one extra outer iteration per stress component
options.D: It avoids all iterative solution by inverting the full voxel operator

questions.rationale: The authors emphasize that the modified operator preserves the original variational solution workflow and convergence effort.
questions.evidence_quote: it does not require additional iterations compared to the strain control version

questions.question: What null-frequency treatment is used in the original strain-control projector, and why?

options.A: A zero fourth-order tensor, to remove the mean field and enforce fluctuation compatibility
options.B: A fourth-order identity, to prescribe the mean strain
options.C: The material tangent, to accelerate Newton convergence
options.D: A scalar zero only for stress components

questions.rationale: The original projection annihilates the average field; the stress-control variant changes this behavior.
questions.evidence_quote: the projection should be a zero fourth order tensor in the null frequency

questions.question: In the hyperelastic particle-reinforced benchmark, how were the particles and voxelized RVE specified?

options.A: Four stiff spherical particles at volume fraction 0.2 in a 64³-voxel cube; particle moduli were 10 times the matrix values
options.B: Eight soft ellipsoids at volume fraction 0.1 in a 32³ cube; moduli were half the matrix
options.C: One central particle at volume fraction 0.5 in a 64² sheet; moduli were 100 times larger
options.D: Around 200 spherical particles at volume fraction 0.2 in a 128³ cube; moduli were equal

questions.rationale: The first benchmark uses four particles and a 64³ discretization, with matrix μ=28 Pa, k=46.67 Pa and particles tenfold stiffer.
questions.evidence_quote: The RVE contains 4 particles occupying a volume fraction of 0.2 and the domain is discretized using 643 voxels

questions.question: Why do the stress- and mixed-control hyperelastic paths (cases 1 and 2) produce superposed macroscopic stress responses, unlike full strain control?

options.A: The hyperelastic material is path independent and cases 1 and 2 share the same path and endpoint
options.B: The Newton solver forces all cases to use the same strain path
options.C: The transverse stresses are prescribed identically in all three cases
options.D: Case 2 uses a lower particle stiffness that cancels path effects

questions.rationale: The stress-controlled ramp follows the same constitutive path as the mixed-control solution, whereas full strain control takes a different path.
questions.evidence_quote: Being the behavior of the hyperelastic material path independent, the macroscopic stress of cases (1) and (2) are superposed

questions.question: What did the polycrystal comparison show about the common pseudo-uniaxial strain-control approximation?

options.A: It produced nonzero compressive transverse stresses that grew with strain, unlike a real uniaxial stress test
options.B: It exactly reproduced uniaxial stress but required more voxels
options.C: It eliminated rate dependence and reduced all stresses to zero
options.D: It matched the stress-controlled response because plasticity is path independent

questions.rationale: Case 4 controls the full deformation gradient with an isochoric-like transverse adjustment; its transverse response differs substantially from true uniaxial stress.
questions.evidence_quote: the compressive transverse stresses are not zero and grow with the applied strain

questions.question: What convergence tolerances were used for the linear and Newton solvers in the performance comparison?

options.A: 10⁻⁸ for the linear solver residual and 10⁻⁶ for relative maximum deformation-gradient correction
options.B: 10⁻⁶ for the linear residual and 10⁻⁸ for Newton corrections

questions.rationale: The performance section specifies separate criteria and tolerances for the two iterative solvers.
questions.evidence_quote: The tolerances used are 10−8 and 10−6 for linear and Newton solvers respectively.

questions.question: What caveat does the paper give for interpreting the polycrystal timing advantage of the full stress-ramp case?

options.A: Its speedup came from many elastic increments under a fixed time step; adaptive stepping would make total times more similar
options.B: It used fewer grains, so timing cannot compare algorithms
options.C: The advantage applies only to hyperelasticity, not plasticity
options.D: It resulted from relaxing the linear solver tolerance in case 2

questions.rationale: Most stress-ramp steps remained elastic and cheap; the authors say adaptive time stepping would yield similar total times.
questions.evidence_quote: this is a consequence of using a fixed time step and, for adaptive time stepping, all the cases will require very similar simulation times
